newsitem.title: CHINA: China needs to set up 81 power firms in 2000-2010.
newsitem.headline: China needs to set up 81 power firms in 2000-2010.

text.p: China needs to establish 81 coal-fired power plants between 2000 and 2010 to meet rising domestic electricity demand, the Science and Technology Daily said on Friday.
The generating capacity of each of the 81 plants would be 2,000 megawatts, the newspaper quoted Power Industry Minister Shi Dazhen as saying.
China's current electricity output per capita was about 880 kilowatt hours while the population would rise to 1.42 billion by 2010 from about 1.3 billion now, Shi said.
China, facing growing demand for energy as its economy expands, depends overwhelmingly on coal for its electric power generation.
However, China must develop several alternative forms of energy in the next century to meet domestic demand, such as nuclear, wind and solar power, Shi said but gave no further details.
China generated 261.076 billion kilowatt hours of electricity in the first quarter, up by 4.23 percent compared with the year-ago period.
